newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany pledges full support for U.N. reform plans.
newsitem.headline: Germany pledges full support for U.N. reform plans.

text.p: Germany on Thursday applauded the sweeping reforms plans for the United Nations bureaucracy announced by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan and promised to fully support the measures.
Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said Annan was sending a positive signal and that it was now up to the 185 U.N. member nations to throw their support behind the proposals.

"We cannot allow the impetus that the Secretary-General has given to the reform with his report to be talked to death," Kinkel said in a statement. "We need a slimmed down, efficient U.N. today more than ever."
Annan presented a series of proposals to streamline the bureaucracy and urged governments to cut back programmes they were responsible for instituting.
"The reforms of such a huge organisation as the U.N. obviously cannot take place overnight," Kinkel said.

"There has been talk about the need for reform for years. Secretary-General Annan has done his share of the work. Now the 185 member states have to use the 52nd general assembly in September to back the reform measures."
